Article Title: ‘No law bars eating chicken over Ganga’: SC judge flags delayed bail at NLIU lecture
Article Text:
File photo: Justice Ujjwal Bhuyan

Bar and Bench

Raises concerns over delayed bail, restrictive conditions

Refers to Bombay HC order on Gaza protest

Calls for scrutiny of judicial decisions

Similar concerns raised earlier

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the courts impose less restrictive conditions when granting bail related to protests? Yes, it's necessary No, they should remain strict 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Saturday questioned the criminalisation of ordinary activities while highlighting delays in granting relief to citizens facing criminal action for protest or dissent, saying there is "no law prohibiting consumption of chicken over the Ganga river. "Speaking at the Justice GP Singh 4th Memorial Lecture at the National Law Institute University (NLIU) in Bhopal, Justice Bhuyan cited the arrest of 14 Muslim men who were accused of consuming chicken biryani while breaking their Ramzan fast on a boat in the Ganga as an example of what he described as the criminalisation of normal activities."Take for example the case of a group of youngsters breaking their fast over the river Ganga by consuming chicken biryani. I am sure consuming chicken biryani is not an offence. It can't be an offence. There is no law prohibiting consumption of chicken over the Ganga river. They were arrested for that very reason and they had to remain in jail for 3 months," he said, as quoted byJustice Bhuyan said such cases also highlighted broader concerns over how courts deal with petitions filed by citizens accused in protest-related cases.He observed that while courts often grant bail or other relief, it frequently comes after considerable delay and is accompanied by restrictive conditions.The judge said the space for expressing divergent opinions in India was shrinking and cautioned against the criminalisation of peaceful democratic activities."It will not be an exaggeration to say that public space for expressing divergent opinion is shrinking in India. The right to express one's views and to demonstrate peacefully are fundamental freedoms of the citizens. Debate and dissent are the essence of democracy. Unfortunately, even normal activities are being criminalised," he said.Justice Bhuyan also questioned the nature of conditions imposed while granting bail, suggesting that some restrictions could have a chilling effect on citizens exercising their right to dissent."These issues raise serious questions. Citizens are finding that though the courts are responsive and do grant bail, do grant relief, many a times it is belated. But it is the restrictive conditions which are imposed while granting bail that are causing the greatest concern. By such restrictive orders, are the courts indirectly telling the citizens or discouraging the citizens not to express their dissent?" he said.He also cited cases where courts granted bail but directed accused persons not to attend public meetings, post on social media or leave the country, saying such conditions could undermine fundamental freedoms.Justice Bhuyan also referred to a July 2025 Bombay high court order dismissing a petition filed by the Communist Party of India (Marxist), which had sought permission to hold a protest at Mumbai's Azad Maidan against the alleged genocide in Gaza.The high court had observed, "Our country has enough issues. We don't want anything like this. I am sorry to say, you are all short-sighted. You are looking at issues in Gaza and Palestine. Look at your own country. Be patriots. This is not patriotism. People say they are patriots."Commenting on the order, Justice Bhuyan said he found it "very amusing" that a judge questioned why citizens wished to protest over developments outside India.Justice Bhuyan said the judiciary is not above criticism and stressed that judgments should be critically examined by lawyers, students and the wider legal community."Judgments, after being delivered, are required to be critically examined and criticised if necessary. Criticism of a judgment does not amount to criticism of a judge."Referring to recent Supreme Court decisions, including the verdict on reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), he encouraged students to analyse judgments critically rather than accepting them unquestioningly."If everybody goes and tells the judges, 'Sir, wonderful thing. Sir, what you say is excellent. Sir, you are a jurist,' then how will the system improve?" he said.Justice Bhuyan also said judges should regularly introspect if they wish to retain public confidence in the institution."For the judges and the judiciary to remain legitimate and to remain relevant, public perception is most crucial... It is not for us to make that comment. It is for the citizens to assess. Perception of the citizens as to where the judiciary stands today, more particularly the Supreme Court, 75 years after we have become a Republic, is what matters," he said.He added that institutional improvement depends on introspection and that robust public debate, including criticism of judicial decisions, strengthens democratic institutions.Justice Bhuyan has previously voiced similar concerns about shrinking space for debate and dissent.Speaking at a Supreme Court Bar Association conference in Bengaluru earlier this year, he said a developed India would require greater tolerance for diverse views and cautioned against criminalising dissent.During that address, he also questioned the extensive use of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), pointing to low conviction rates and arguing that prolonged incarceration without timely trials could not be a model for a developed nation.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan spoke at the Justice GP Singh 4th Memorial Lecture at the National Law Institute University (NLIU) in Bhopal. He said the space for expressing divergent opinions in India was shrinking and cautioned against the criminalisation of peaceful democratic activities. He also highlighted delays in granting relief to citizens facing criminal action for protest or dissent.

Article Title: 'Misrepresents statement': MEA fact-checks viral claim on spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal's remarks on CJP protests
Article Text:
MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the claims of foreign funding behind the CJP protests are justified? Yes, there is a basis for these claims No, the claims are unfounded 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Sunday termed as "misleading" a social media post claiming that ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said there was no foreign funding behind the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led youth protest in Delhi.The CJP stir, followed by demonstrations in other parts of the country, led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET (UG) question paper leak and other related issues."The post is misleading and misrepresents the statement of the spokesperson," the MEA's fact-check unit wrote on X, referring to the statement attributed to Jaiswal.It also shared Jaiswal's actual response to a query on allegations of foreign funding behind the CJP-led demonstrations."Madhu, regarding the point you raised about allegations of foreign funding and other such claims in connection with the ongoing protests, I would like to say that I do not have any information on this matter to share with you at this time," he replied during a weekly media briefing on Friday.The clarification came in response to a viral post on X claiming that Jaiswal had said, "I have been asked about the funding of the CJP protest many a time.I want to say that our intelligence & investigation reveals there is no foreign funding in it."CJP, an online satirical platform, was formed following a remark by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, in which he described a section of unemployed youth as "cockroaches." The CJI later clarified that he had been misquoted.The allegations of foreign funding have largely been linked to the fact that Abhijit Dipke, who founded the outfit, is a former student of Boston University. Dipke founded CJP in Boston and returned to India in June to lead its demonstrations seeking accountability over the NEET (UG) paper leak in May.The demonstrations peaked on July 20 with the group's "Chalo Sansad" march to Parliament, where protesters faced police action. The crackdown drew criticism from opposition parties, while the police maintained that the protest had turned violent.The 37-day-long agitation culminated in Pradhan's resignation on Saturday afternoon. The CJP called off its stir after the government accepted all its demands.Union minister Pralhad Joshi has been assigned additional charge of Pradhan's ministry of human resource development.
Article Summary: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Sunday termed as "misleading" a social media post claiming that ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said there was no foreign funding behind the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led youth protest in Delhi. The CJP stir, followed by demonstrations in other parts of the country, led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Article Title: 'This is a new subject for me': Pralhad Joshi after taking charge as education minister
Article Text:
Joshi thanks PM Modi, says he accepts responsibility with humility

Assigned additional charge after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most pressing issue Joshi should address in education? Examination irregularities Improving quality of education Transparency in educational policies 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Change comes amid protests over examination irregularities

NEW DELHI: Union minister Pralhad Joshi on Sunday assumed charge as the Union education minister, a day after President Droupadi Murmu accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan and assigned him the additional responsibility of the ministry. Taking charge, Joshi said he was reviewing the ministry's functioning and familiarising himself with the department, describing education as "a new subject" for him.Speaking to reporters after assuming office, Joshi said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had entrusted him with the responsibility and that he would take time to understand the ministry before making detailed comments."The Prime Minister has entrusted me with this responsibility with full confidence.I was in Karnataka yesterday. I reached here last night and came this morning to take charge. I have assumed charge. I am reviewing all the details here and the decisions that need to be taken. I have been gathering information and trying to understand the functioning of the entire ministry. We had continuous meetings today. This is a new subject for me. I have taken charge today and held detailed discussions with the senior officers.It is a very big department, so I will speak to you in detail after I have understood it completely," Joshi said.Soon after taking charge, Joshi shared a message on X thanking Prime Minister Narendra Modi for entrusting him with the Education Ministry."Today, I assumed charge as the Union Minister for Education. I am grateful to Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji for placing his faith in me and entrusting me with this responsibility," he wrote.He added, "I accept it with humility and a deep sense of duty."Joshi was given charge of the Education ministry on Saturday after President Droupadi Murmu accepted Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation from the Union council of ministers with immediate effect.According to a Rashtrapati Bhavan statement, Joshi will continue to hold his existing portfolios while also heading the Education Ministry."The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio," the statement said.Joshi is currently the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and New and Renewable Energy. He has previously served as the Union Minister for Coal, Mines and Parliamentary Affairs.The change at the top of the education ministry comes after weeks of nationwide student protests over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, including the NEET paper leak. Students have been demanding greater transparency, accountability and reforms in the examination system.Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation on Saturday, saying he had submitted it to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the ongoing protests over examination irregularities were not exploited by "anti-national forces."Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) announced that it had withdrawn its 36-day-long agitation at Jantar Mantar in "good faith" after Pradhan stepped down from the Union council of ministers and the organisation received assurances from the government on its other demands.
Article Summary: Pralhad Joshi assumed charge of the Education ministry on Sunday. President Droupadi Murmu accepted Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on Saturday. Joshi will continue to hold his existing portfolios while heading the Education Ministry. Change comes amid protests over examination irregularities and reforms.

Article Title: 'Take lesson from Jantar Mantar': Mehbooba Mufti hits out at Yogi Adityanath over demolition order for Jauhar University buildings
Article Text:
Mohammad Ali Jauhar University campus in Rampur.

NEW DELHI: Targeting Yogi Adityanath over the proposed demolition of 38 buildings at senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan 's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Mehbooba Mufti on Sunday said the Uttar Pradesh chief minister should "take a lesson from Jantar Mantar."The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president was referring to the youth-led protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, which led to Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged NEET (UG) question paper leak and other education-related issues."Destroying an institution of learning like Jauhar University displays nothing but hatred and vengeance. Yogi should take a lesson from Jantar Mantar and see how the youth of this country are rejecting the politics of hate and division.Stand with the protesting students," she wrote on X.Mufti was responding to a post by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, who said that the party's MPs and MLAs were taking part in a protest by students seeking to "save" Jauhar University in Rampur."The 'Protect Education' movement will also triumph! To encourage the students who have sat on a dharna to save Jauhar University in Rampur, our MPs and MLAs are participating," Yadav wrote in his post.Questioning the Uttar Pradesh government's stand, he asked why the constructions at Jauhar University could not be regularised when similar structures were allegedly regularised through administrative orders."If the BJP government can regularise other constructions based on the UP government's administrative order, then why not Jauhar University? Why this discrimination and malice against Jauhar University?" the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister asked.The SP has demanded that the proposed demolition be halted, alleging that the move would adversely impact the future of students."Our collective demand is that the BJP should not throw the future of our youth into the fire of its vengeance," Yadav stated.The remarks come amid a proposed demolition drive at Mohammad Ali Jauhar University after the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) ordered the removal of 38 allegedly unauthorised buildings on the campus.The RDA issued a notice to the Jauhar Trust, which runs the university, on June 28, alleging that 82,309.80 square metres of construction within the campus had been carried out illegally. According to the authority, 38 blocks were built without approved building maps, while only two structures had received prior permission from the District Panchayat.The authority alleged that the secretary of the Jauhar Trust failed to submit approval documents within the stipulated period. It granted the trust an additional 15 days to remove the 38 structures, warning that demolition proceedings would be initiated if it failed to comply.The demolition order was issued by the RDA vice-chairman, who also serves as the Rampur District Magistrate, under provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973.
Article Summary: Mehbooba Mufti says Yogi Adityanath should "take a lesson from Jantar Mantar" Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister was referring to the youth-led protests at Delhi's Jantr Mantar. She was responding to a post by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, who said that the party's MPs and MLAs were taking part in a protest by students.

Article Title: 'PM Modi's apology awaited': Opposition to keep up NEET protest pressure in Parliament
Article Text:
File photo: Opposition & ruling party MPs staged counter-protests & raised slogans against each other outside Parliament on Thursday (Picture credit: PTI)

Rahul Gandhi seeks answers from Amit Shah

Opposition to decide stand on anti-paper leak bill

NEW DELHI: The Congress-led opposition is set to keep up the pressure on the government in Parliament over the alleged police brutality against students protesting the NEET-UG paper leak, with demands for action against those responsible for the assault and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sources quoted by news agency PTI said on Sunday.The opposition's floor strategy, including its stand on the proposed amendment to the anti-paper leak law, will be finalised at a meeting of INDIA bloc leaders in Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's chamber on Monday morning, the sources said.The developments come ahead of what is expected to be a heated debate in Parliament over the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, which has been listed for introduction, consideration and passage in the Lok Sabha on Monday.Ahead of the Parliament session, leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah, demanding accountability for what he described as the "barbaric assault" on peacefully protesting students and questioning whether the home minister had authorised the use of "lethal force", including pellet guns.In the letter, the Congress MP said peaceful protest is a cornerstone of democracy and it is the government's responsibility to protect protesters and address their grievances through dialogue."Such brutal violence destroys every norm, and has outraged the country. Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability. Their voice will be heard," he wrote.Sharing the letter on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Gandhi had asked Shah two questions: "As the Home Minister, did you authorise the use of lethal force, including pellet guns, against students? If not, who granted this authorisation? Are the individuals seen raining blows on students while dressed in plain clothes, police personnel or volunteers? Who authorised their deployment?""The home minister must answer these crucial questions in Parliament tomorrow. The prime minister should apologise to the students," Ramesh added.Rahul had earlier alleged that security personnel used pellet guns, tear gas and batons against peaceful protesters during the July 20 march to Parliament.He also referred to 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab, claiming the youth could lose an eye after allegedly being struck by pellets. Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns during the protest, while the CRPF has not responded to the allegation.The Congress has described education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as a victory for students but has maintained that Prime Minister Modi should also apologise over the alleged police action.Kharge has said it is now the prime minister's turn to apologise and take strict action against those responsible for using lathis, batons and pellet guns against protesting students.After Pradhan's resignation, Rahul also urged PM Modi to apologise to students "out of respect for the future of the country" and for the alleged "atrocities" committed during the protests."This is not the end. We still await the prime minister's apology to our students," Ramesh said, reiterating the demand for accountability for those responsible for the alleged excesses.A heated debate on the paper leak issue is likely if the government and opposition can resolve the ongoing deadlock in both Houses of Parliament.The opposition will also decide whether to support the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.The proposed legislation seeks to tighten punishments for examination-related offences. Individuals involved in paper leaks or other unfair means would face imprisonment ranging from five to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 50 lakh. Organised crimes related to examination fraud would attract a minimum seven-year jail term and fines of up to Rs 10 crore.The existing law prescribes imprisonment of three to five years for cheating-related offences, while organised exam fraud currently attracts five to 10 years in prison and a minimum fine of Rs 1 crore.Asked on Saturday whether the Congress would support the new bill, Rahul said the party would take a decision only after consultations with other opposition parties."The Congress party has a central principle. We will decide this during a meeting of opposition parties and a decision will be based on opposition consensus. In Parliament, that is our discipline, and that is our way of functioning," he said.The government announced the proposed amendments after student protests over the NEET-UG paper leak intensified across the country. Prime Minister Modi has also promised fast-track courts and stricter punishment for those involved in paper leak cases.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which spearheaded the agitation, called off its 36-day protest on Saturday after the resignation of the education minister and the government's acceptance of its other demands.
Article Summary: Opposition to decide stand on anti-paper leak bill on Monday, sources say. Opposition will also decide whether to support the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. Opposition demands action against those responsible for the assault and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: 'Beginning of accountability': Prashant Kishor on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Prashant Kishor said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder and Bankipur assembly by-election candidate Prashant Kishor on Sunday described Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as the "beginning of accountability", asserting that sustained public pressure had compelled the government to act.Addressing reporters, Kishor said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations and demonstrated that public mobilisation could force those in power to respond."This is the beginning of accountability. Accountability is being enforced under public pressure. I always say that in this country, the opposition party can be weak. The opposition cannot be weak," he said.Expressing support for those opposing what he termed the government's "undemocratic behaviour", Kishor said the issue was larger than any single political party."We stand with anyone who wants to challenge this government's undemocratic behaviour and their work. Sonam Wangchuk is my friend. He's a prominent academic, environmentalist, and friend of ours. This isn't about a party; people have seen that if people stand up, if the public rises, even those in power will have to bow down," he said.Referring to the ongoing protests in Delhi, Kishor said they reflected widespread public anger rather than the agenda of any one organisation."What you and I are seeing in Delhi wasn't a protest by one Sonam Wangchuk. The thousands of people who came to protest didn't carry CJP flags. They were ordinary young people, frustrated by the daily paper leaks, unemployment, and the crumbling education system," he said.Commenting on the arrest of Janshakti Janata Dal national president Tej Pratap Yadav, Kishor alleged that the action reflected the government's nervousness."Tej Pratap announced his support yesterday, and at 1.30 am last night, Tej Pratap was arrested and sent to Beur Jail. This shows how scared these people are. Under what section was he arrested? Why was he arrested? The police administration should explain this," he was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.Kishor claimed Pradhan's resignation was only the beginning and suggested that the agitation would continue."Dharmendra Pradhan had to leave, and that's not all, this is just the beginning. This isn't going to stop," he added.Kishor also raised objections to an order issued by the district magistrate regarding election awareness activities involving Jeevika Didis. He urged the election commission and its observers to take note of the matter and initiate action."The District Magistrate issued order. In which he stated that Jeevika Didi, would work for election awareness. We hope that the Election Commission, their observers, will take cognizance of this matter, and take action," he said.He warned that if no action was taken by Monday, he and his supporters would stage a protest outside the Election Commission's office."If action isn't taken by tomorrow, we will go to the Election Commission and sit on a protest at their gate, along with my colleagues," Kishor said.
Article Summary: Jan Suraaj founder and Bankipur assembly by-election candidate Prashant Kishor described Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as the "beginning of accountability" He said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations and demonstrated that public mobilisation could force those in power to respond.

Article Title: Assam floods: Death toll reaches 66; BJP launches Rs 12 crore relief drive - top developments
Article Text:
Floodwaters inundate several parts of Assam, affecting lakhs of residents across multiple districts. (ANI images)

BJP targets Rs 12 crore for relief material

Flood situation improves as waters recede

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the Assam government is doing enough to support flood-affected families? Yes, absolutely No, more needs to be done 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Death toll reaches 66 as four more people die

Relief operations continue across affected districts

PM Modi reviews flood situation for second consecutive day

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Sunday said the death toll from this year's floods has risen to 66 even as the flood situation showed signs of improvement across the state with water levels receding in several affected districts. More than 6.54 lakh people continue to be affected across six districts, while the state BJP has launched a Rs 12 crore relief campaign to provide clothing to flood-hit families.Addressing the media, Sarma confirmed that 66 people have died in the floods, including one person in Guwahati Urban. "So far, 66 persons, including one person in Guwahati Urban, have died in floods in the state," he said.The chief minister announced that the Assam BJP would distribute two lakh Mekhela-Chadors to women and clothes to two lakh children affected by the floods in some of the worst-hit districts. He appealed to party workers to actively participate in relief efforts and contribute towards the fundraising campaign.Sarma said the party aims to raise Rs 12 crore to procure relief material for flood victims, particularly women and children in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat and Jorhat districts."I appeal to all BJP workers of Assam to get involved in flood relief operations. From the Assam State BJP, we have decided to provide 2 lakh Mekhela-Chador to 2 lakh women and clothes to 2 lakh children who have been affected by the flood.We need Rs 12 crore for it," he said.The chief minister also outlined how party members could contribute to the initiative."I appeal to the BJP Karyakartas, who want to donate below Rs 2000, to give the amount to their local MLAs, and those who want to donate above Rs 2000 can deposit their cheques to the party's account number, and we will give the account number on social media," Sarma added.Expressing confidence that the target would be achieved within days, Sarma said support had already begun pouring in from BJP workers across Assam and other parts of the country."We have targeted to collect Rs 12 crore for it. BJP Karyakartas will help to collect this amount. BJP Karyakartas from various parts of Assam and outside Assam have assured us to help us. We are very much hopeful that within the next 4-5 days we will be able to collect this amount and to help the flood-affected people of Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat, and Jorhat districts," he said.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the flood situation improved on Sunday as water levels receded in most flood-hit areas of Upper Assam after rainfall stopped in many parts of the state.Officials said the improvement was particularly visible in Charaideo, Sivasagar and Jorhat districts, raising hopes that relief operations would become more effective."We hope the situation would improve further during the day. This would help us provide relief in a better way," an ASDMA official said.Despite the improvement, more than 6,54,800 people remain affected in Charaideo, Dibrugarh, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar districts.Sivasagar remains the worst-affected district with nearly 2.9 lakh people impacted, followed by Charaideo with around 1.9 lakh and Jorhat with approximately 1.3 lakh affected residents.The number of affected people has declined from over 7.05 lakh across nine districts recorded on Friday, indicating a gradual improvement in the overall flood situation.ASDMA's latest flood bulletin said four more people died in the past 24 hours, taking this year's flood death toll to 66. Three of the fatalities were reported from Sivasagar district and one from Charaideo.The authority said 810 villages remain submerged while floodwaters have damaged 34,970.8 hectares of agricultural land across the state.Floods have also damaged embankments, roads, bridges and other public infrastructure in several districts. The Dikhow River at Sivasagar and the Dhansiri River at Numaligarh continue to flow above the danger mark.Authorities said 274 relief camps and distribution centres are currently operational across six districts, sheltering 18,902 displaced people.Rescue operations are being carried out jointly by the Army, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Fire and Emergency Services, Assam Police and civil administration.During the past 24 hours, the state administration distributed 1,668.68 quintals of rice, 286.99 quintals of dal, 83.75 quintals of salt and 7,995.01 litres of mustard oil among flood-affected families.Chief Minister Sarma said the administration had now been able to reach almost all flood-hit areas as water levels gradually receded. He also confirmed that an inter-ministerial central team had arrived in Assam to assess the damage caused by floods in Upper Assam.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday spoke to Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal to review the flood situation in Assam, a day after speaking with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and assuring the state of full central support.Sharing details of the conversation on X, Sonowal said the prime minister enquired about the ground situation while he was visiting flood-hit areas in Dibrugarh."I am currently in Dibrugarh, visiting the affected areas, assessing the ground situation and standing with our affected brothers and sisters," Sonowal said.He added that an inter-ministerial team had already reached Assam and was visiting the affected districts to assess the damage."The Modi Government stands shoulder-to-shoulder with the people of Assam and has assured all necessary support for relief and rehabilitation. I extend my deepest gratitude to PM Modi ji for his constant concern and unwavering support," Sonowal added.Earlier on Saturday, Sonowal reviewed relief operations at camps in flood-affected areas and directed officials to ensure uninterrupted access to healthcare, food, drinking water and other essential services for displaced residents.
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the death toll from this year's floods has risen to 66. More than 6.54 lakh people continue to be affected across six districts. The state BJP has launched a Rs 12 crore relief campaign to provide clothing to flood-hit families.

Article Title: 'Jamaati fundamentalists involved': Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari alleges 'foreign hand' in Kolkata rally violence
Article Text:
A student protest rally turned violent in Kolkata on Friday (PTI)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday alleged that the violence during a protest rally in Kolkata over the NEET question paper leak was orchestrated by "Islamic fundamentalists," claiming they may have been supported by "foreign forces. "Adhikari made the remarks while speaking to reporters in Nandigram after attending a programme to commemorate Kargil Vijay Diwas, marking the 27th anniversary of India's victory over Pakistan in the 1999 Kargil War.Claiming that those involved in the violence had no connection to the student-led agitation, he said, "There is no connection between these people and the movement. They are not students. They are Jamaati (Islamic) fundamentalists. Probe agencies will determine whether foreign forces backed them.""The violence may have been fuelled by resentment over several decisions of the BJP government in the state, including action against unregistered madrassas, implementation of court directions relating to OBC certificates, enforcement of cattle slaughter laws and measures to curb noise pollution," he added.Referring to the assault on a journalist during the protest, Adhikari alleged that media personnel were "deliberately targeted" and that there were "attempts on their lives."Clashes erupted between Left-backed protesters and police during the demonstration, prompting security forces to resort to baton charges and fire tear gas shells to disperse the crowd.The West Bengal government invoked its newly enacted anti-goonda law against those accused of orchestrating the violence during the protest, with the chief minister warning that they would face punishment "their next three generations will remember."Adhikari had earlier told the assembly that around 70 people identified from the rally were "not students" and had no connection with the agitation over the alleged NEET question paper leak.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged that the violence during a protest rally in Kolkata over the NEET question paper leak was orchestrated by "Islamic fundamentalists" Claimed that those involved in the violence had no connection to the student-led agitation. Clashes erupted between Left-backed protesters and police during the demonstration.

Article Title: 'He is only interim': Sanjay Raut claims Fadnavis may replace Pralhad Joshi as education minister
Article Text:
'Modi govt had to bow down'

Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Sunday claimed that newly appointed Union education minister Pralhad Joshi's is only 'interim' minister. He alleged that the Centre is searching for a permanent replacement and suggested that Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis could eventually be given the portfolio.Addressing a press conference, Raut said Joshi was better suited to his previous responsibilities and described his current role as interim. "Pralhad Joshi is currently the interim Education Minister. At best, he might make a good Coal Minister. I believe this is a temporary arrangement, and the government is actively searching for a permanent Education Minister," he said.Raut claimed that Fadnavis, because of his educational background and ideological alignment with the RSS, could emerge as the Centre's preferred choice."To my knowledge, Devendra Fadnavis could be the country's best Education Minister. Modi ji has also made up his mind about this. He is aligned with RSS ideology, is well educated and has experience in running a state," he said.However, he added that the decision was being held up because of uncertainty over who would replace Fadnavis as Maharashtra chief minister if he were moved to the Union Cabinet.Raut also launched a fresh attack on the Centre over the student agitation at Jantar Mantar, alleging that police excesses were committed against protesters and holding Union home minister Amit Shah responsible.He further claimed that the Modi government was forced to accept the protesters' demands only after sustained pressure from the youth movement."The Modi government had to bow down to the power of the youth and accept their demands. Governments should remain humble before the people, but humility and restraint have disappeared from the BJP's vocabulary," he said.His remarks come a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister amid the nationwide agitation over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, following which Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the education ministry.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena MP Sanjay Raut says Pralhad Joshi is only 'interim' education minister. Suggests Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis could eventually be given the portfolio. Raut also launched a fresh attack on the Centre over the student agitation at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union education minister a day after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union education minister

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Pralhad Joshi is the right choice for Union Education Minister? Yes No 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Pralhad Joshi on Sunday took charge as Union education minister. This came a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the role amid student protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and nationwide.Earlier, Pradhan shared his resignation letter on X, addressing it to his "young friends". He said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in view of the situation that had unfolded across the country.The CJP-led protest was later called off after a delegation of the group held talks with Union ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh, with both sides reaching a mutual understanding on the protesters' key demands.Born on November 27, 1962, in Bijapur, Karnataka, Pralhad Joshi completed his schooling in Hubballi. He attended Railway School for his primary education and later studied at New English School before graduating with a bachelor's degree in arts from Shri Kadasiddheshwar Arts College, Hubballi.Before joining politics full-time, Joshi was associated with business. He later emerged as a prominent Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader in Karnataka and has represented the Dharwad Lok Sabha constituency since 2004, winning five consecutive terms in Parliament.Over the years, Joshi has held several key organisational and ministerial positions. Between 2019 and 2024, he served as the Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines. Following the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, he was entrusted with the portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy.As Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Joshi has overseen several flagship government initiatives, including the National Green Hydrogen Mission, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM, and programmes aimed at expanding India's renewable energy capacity.
Article Summary: Pralhad Joshi on Sunday took charge as Union education minister. This came a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the role amid student protests. The CJP- led protest was later called off after a delegation of the group held talks with Union ministers.

Article Title: 'Who approved pellet guns?' Rahul Gandhi writes Amit Shah over 'barbaric assault' on students
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi along with a victim of alleged pellet gun firing during a students protest

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most effective way for students to voice their grievances? Peaceful protests Formal petitions Social media campaigns Engaging with politicians 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah , demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students protesting "peacefully" at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20.Calling out the "most shocking" use of "lethal pellet guns," the Congress leader claimed that a 19-year-old student has been undergoing a severe pain and is "likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet guns"."Security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to you, so I ask:1. As Home Minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? 2. Are the people in plain clothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Who authorized their deployment?" Rahul Gandhi wrote in a letter addressed to Amit Shah.The Congress leader futher said that it's "government's responsibility to protect protestors and resolve their grievances through dialogue"."Peaceful protest is crucial to any democracy. It is the government's responsibility to protect protestors and resolve their grievances through dialogue. Such brutal violence destroys every norm, and has outraged the country. Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability.Their voice will be heard," he further wrote.Rahul Gandhi on Saturday slammed the government, saying children protesting for their rights receive "pellets" instead of "justice."In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared a video featuring a youth who was reportedly beaten by the Delhi Police during Monday's protests against paper leaks."Sahil was standing with the Tricolour in his hand, merely asking for a clean, fair exam and the fruit of his hard work--the police raised a gun and badly injured him by firing pellets. This is not British tyranny; it is the brutality of the Modi government in independent India--where innocent students demanding their rights receive pellets instead of justice," the post read.More than 118 police personnel sustained injuries, including senior officers holding the ranks of Special Commissioner of Police, Joint Commissioner of Police, Additional Commissioner of Police, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police, and Assistant Commissioner of Police, along with several female police personnel. During the scuffle, around 60 protesters were also reported to have been injured.On Friday, the Union Cabinet approved amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to strengthen the anti-paper leak law amid continuing nationwide protests over the NEET-UG row, while the deadlock in Parliament continued for the fifth day.According to sources, the proposed amendment Bill is likely to be tabled in Parliament on Monday, July 27.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students protesting "peacefully" at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20. The Congress leader claimed that a 19-year-old student has been undergoing a severe pain and is "likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet guns"

Article Title: Bihar bandh violence: Siwan cop suspended for firing AK-47; 200 NEET protesters detained
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the treatment of minors during detentions? It is unacceptable, they should be protected It's necessary for maintaining order 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PATNA: Nearly 200 students allegedly detained after the July 22 and 25 protests, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak, remained in custody for over 24 hours across police stations in the city, advocates alleged. Meanwhile, a Siwan police personnel was suspended for firing AK-47 during the July 25 bandh violence.Advocate Akanksha Shahi, who is providing legal aid to several detainees, said 58 of them were sent to remand on July 25. Around 87 more are likely to be sent to judicial custody on Sunday, she said. Several detainees are minors, she added.According to advocates, around 15 detainees were held at Gandhi Maidan police station, 28 at Digha, and 22 each at Rupaspura and Airport police stations, among others.Advocate Abhishek Kumar, who is also providing pro bono legal aid (free legal help), said the families of several detainees were not informed about their detention. He said detainees are required to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours, which expired at 2pm on Sunday. The detainees were taken for medical examinations to govt hospitals around 5pm on Sunday, he said.Soma Kumari, a student activist and member of the Disha Students’ Organisation at Airport police station, said, “Over 200 people were detained during the July 25 protest.Around 70% of them are minors. Police are not informing us about the next step.”She added, “This is happening after it was assured by the govt that no action will be taken on the protesting students and all the FIRs will be quashed. But instead of quashing the FIRs, Patna police has kept them.”Families of the detainees said some students were caught while passing through the protest area.Shahi said the police were releasing all the women and minors, while other detainees were being sent to judicial custody.Responding to the allegations, Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma told TOI on Sunday that 86 protesters arrested during the July 25 violence near Gandhi Maidan were sent to judicial custody, while 60 others, including minors and women, were released on personal bonds. He said a case had been registered against the accused at Gandhi Maidan police station.The SSP added that in connection with the July 22 protest, police registered 23 FIRs across different police stations in the city and arrested 67 people, who were sent to judicial custody in different cases.Providing further details of the July 25 violence, Gandhi Maidan SHO Akhilesh Kumar Mishra, who sustained injuries during the clash, said four FIRs were registered in connection with the incident. One FIR was lodged on his statement, another on the statement of a magistrate, a third by the officer in charge of the Gandhi Maidan TOP checkpost that was attacked during the violence, and the fourth on a complaint by a repairman alleging that protesters overturned a govt vehicle parked near the police vehicle garage.Mishra said the accused have been booked under multiple charges, including unlawful assembly, rioting, attempt to murder, obstructing public servants from discharging their duties, and other offences related to the violence. Referring to the July 22 protest, Mishra said four FIRs were also registered at Gandhi Maidan police station, leading to the arrest of five people from the police station’s jurisdiction, while additional arrests were made by other police stations.Meanwhile, ADG (Law and Order) K Suhita Anupam said FIRs were registered in Saran, Siwan, Bhagalpur, Sitamarhi and Jehanabad in connection with violence during the July 25 bandh.She said 56 people were arrested in Saran, 25 in Siwan, 41 named accused in Bhagalpur, 13 in Sitamarhi and 13 in Jehanabad. She added that 19 govt vehicles and one private vehicle were vandalised, while 58 police personnel were injured, adding Siwan personnel who fired an AK-47 had been suspended.
Article Summary: Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma says 86 protesters arrested during the July 25 violence near Gandhi Maidan were sent to judicial custody. 60 others, including minors and women, were released on personal bonds. Siwan police personnel suspended for firing AK-47 during July 25 bandh violence.

Article Title: Opposition MPs take out march in solidarity with protesters
Article Text:
Opposition MPs stage protest against govt at Parliament in black clothes

NEW DELHI: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students, two days after they held a dharna outside the PM's residence and were forcibly evacuated by police.The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. From there, they marched to the Gandhi Smriti holding their phone torches. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman, Supriya Sule, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, N K Premachandran, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Sudhakar Singh, Misa Bharti, Arvind Sawant, Saugata Roy and Mahua Moitra.Rahul said, "We go to remember the students we lost - the children driven to take their own lives after the NEET paper leak.And we go to stand with the students who lie injured today - beaten for peacefully demanding justice and accountability. India's students are not alone. The entire opposition stands with them and their demands."Congress's P Chidambaram said, "All roads are barricaded, and hundreds of policemen are mobilised to 'secure' the roads of Delhi. What is govt afraid of? Why this sense of panic?" Earlier, Congress rubbished PM Modi's statement assuring the protesting youth. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the students don't need platitudes after govt used pellet guns, shock batons and tear gas on them.
Article Summary: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students. The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman and Supriya Sule.

Article Title: Bengaluru road rage: Cabbie confronts rash driver, ends up clinging to bonnet for 1km - video
Article Text: BENGALURU: A cab driver’s reckless road rage created panic in the neighbourhood after he tried to mow down another cab driver who confronted him over rash driving. The terrifying incident ended with the victim clinging to the car’s bonnet for nearly a kilometre before locals intervened.According to police, cab driver Ananth, a resident of Laggere, was driving recklessly in Chowdeshwari Nagar around 11pm Friday. Concerned by his dangerous driving, a fellow cab driver, Manjunath , from Mahalakshmi Layout, intercepted the vehicle and questioned Ananth’s behaviour. Manjunath also called police control room to report the incident.Enraged by the complaint, Ananth accelerated his car towards Manjunath in an apparent attempt to run him over.In the chaos, Manjunath was thrown onto the bonnet of the moving vehicle. Instead of stopping, Ananth continued driving for nearly a kilometre with Manjunath desperately clinging to the bonnet, putting his life at risk. Ananth also ran over a stray dog, which sustained injuries.Locals chased the speeding car, eventually intercepting and forcing it to stop. They accused him of driving under the influence of alcohol. However, before police could arrive, Ananth abandoned the vehicle and fled. Ananth appeared before police Saturday evening. He was subjected to an alcometer test, and the result was negative.Manjunath and Ananth reached a compromise on Sunday and did not file any complaint. “So, we fined Ananth for reckless driving and imposed a fine of Rs 3,000,” a senior officer said.
Article Summary: Cab driver Ananth was driving recklessly in Chowdeshwari Nagar around 11pm Friday. Concerned by his dangerous driving, a fellow cab driver, Manjunath, intercepted the vehicle and questioned Ananth's behaviour. Enraged by the complaint, Ananth accelerated his car towards Man junath in an apparent attempt to run him over. In the chaos, Man Junath was thrown onto the bonnet of the moving vehicle.

Article Title: Delhi Police claims only 3,000 cops present for 10,000 protesters, file 15 FIRs
Article Text:
Delhi police uses facial recognition system at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.Police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered in connection with the agitation, according to Delhi Police sources. The police also said around 65 students sustained injuries during the demonstrations.The Delhi Police further said it is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements" visiting Jantar Mantar.According to police sources, more than 2,000 people with criminal records who had visited the protest site have been identified so far, as cited by ANI.This is not the first time the Delhi Police has deployed Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras.The force has previously used the technology as part of security arrangements during Republic Day, Independence Day, Holi, Diwali, Eid, Ramlila celebrations and several other major public events across the city.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan would continue without interruption.On Friday, Dipke welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike but reiterated that the movement would continue until its demand for accountability over the examination irregularities is met."Our demonstration will go on until Dharmendra Pradhan steps down. Any meeting must take place at a neutral location or venue. Nothing less than the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan will be accepted," he said.Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk questioned why his commitment to the cause required a "character certificate".Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.The activist said he had earlier been offered verbal assurances but insisted on a written commitment, which delayed the end of his fast by two days.Following a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, representatives of CJP said the government had sought time until Saturday afternoon to consider their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Delhi police deploy 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order at Jantar Mantar. Police sources say around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered. Delhi Police is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements"

Article Title: 'First it hurt me, later I took advantage': FM Nirmala Sitharaman's paper leak remarks spark political row
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has come under fire over her remarks on the NEET paper leak controversy after she said some students had used the additional time before the re-examination to improve their performance. The remarks drew sharp criticism from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders, who accused her of being "insensitive" to students impacted by the alleged leaks.Speaking to news agency ANI, Sitharaman defended the government's handling of the paper leak controversy, saying its response had ensured timely arrests, re-examinations and declaration of results.Sitharaman said the government's response included timely arrests, a re-examination and prompt declaration of results. She said some students had used the additional preparation time to improve their performance, adding, "First it sort of hurt me when the paper leakages happened but later I took advantage of that and prepared even more and my performance has improved and I've done well." She added that such students had "taken this challenge and faced this, and come out bright in bright colours," while asserting that "the government is responding, PM is responding.Sitharaman also accused the Congress of disrupting Parliament despite the government's willingness to discuss the issue.The FM also accused the Congress of disrupting Parliament despite the government's willingness to hold a discussion on the issue. She said the government had agreed to the Opposition's demand for a debate, but the opposition keeps disrupting the house. "The government is willing to have full-fledged discussion in the House, come discuss," she said, accusing the Congress of "disruption of the House" because "the truth will come out, and the government's actions will be placed before the House. They don't want a fair discussion."The remarks come as thousands of students have been protesting for weeks over the alleged NEET paper leaks, with demonstrations centred at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and echoed in several parts of the country. On July 20, protesters marching towards Parliament were lathi-charged and tear-gassed by police and the rapid action force, leaving several students as well as security personnel injured.The government has since reached out to protesters, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi promising strict action against those responsible for paper leaks and Union ministers holding talks with activist Sonam Wangchuk and the representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party.The CJP strongly objected to Sitharaman's remarks, arguing that they trivialised the impact of the controversy on students.The remarks also triggered widespread reactions on social media, with several users criticising Sitharaman's comments as 'deeply insensitive', while accusing the government of downplaying the impact of the paper leak controversy on students.Reacting to her statement, CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka said, "By this logic, every paper in this country should get leaked."In a post on X, the organisation's official handle wrote, "The Finance Minister is claiming NEET students took advantage of the paper leak and worked harder for the re-NEET.Now we're extolling the virtues of paper leaks? This is a shockingly insensitive comment when 20 students have died by suicide because of YOUR incompetence! Shame."The remarks also drew sharp reactions from Opposition leaders. Congress leader Supriya Shrinate took a swipe at Sitharaman, asking her to "please list the benefits" for the 22 students who allegedly died by suicide following the paper leak controversy.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra also reacted on X, writing, "Honestly this entire Cabinet should resign."
Article Summary: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has come under fire over her remarks on the NEET paper leak controversy. She said some students had used the additional time before the re-examination to improve their performance. The remarks drew sharp criticism from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders, who accused her of being "insensitive"

Article Title: CJP launches website, invites proof against ‘police excesses’
Article Text:
CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Friday launched a dedicated website inviting protesters to upload photographs and videos of police personnel who allegedly assaulted demonstrators during and after the July 20 Sansad Chalo march, saying it would identify the officers and pursue legal action against them.Launching the portal at Jantar Mantar, CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.“We will go through every photograph and video, verify them, identify the police personnel involved and file complaints against them. We will demand registration of FIRs against such officers. If FIRs are not registered, we will approach the courts. Lawyers from across the country have come forward to help us and we will obtain court orders to ensure cases are registered,” CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said.He said the organisation will prepare a list of officers allegedly involved in the clampdown and “ensure they are punished till the end”.Besides reiterating its demand for action against the cops allegedly involved, CJP has also sought a public apology from the Delhi police commissioner, Rapid Action Force head and the Centre.“We request that all these demands be accepted at the earliest, failing which the movement will only grow bigger and spread across the country,” CJP said in a letter submitted to Centre Friday.It also sought an assurance that protesters would not be targeted in future, and said in-principal approval for this demand was given by Centre’s representatives who met the CJP spokespersons Friday.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Friday launched a dedicated website inviting protesters to upload photographs and videos of police personnel who allegedly assaulted demonstrators during and after the Sansad Chalo march. CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.

Article Title: NATO-backed scientists planted 13-foot-tall giant grass on war-damaged land near Bucha, hoping its roots can help clean Ukraine's polluted soil
Article Text:
Scientists prepare a field for Miscanthus plants in northern Czech Republic (AFP photo)

Breadbasket of Europe

Poll Vote & Share your view How important is it to develop natural methods for soil restoration in war-affected areas? Very important Not important 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Testing giant Miscanthus

A Ukrainian fighter walks past a burning wheat field (Reuters file photo)

How grass helps soil

Improving soil naturally

A Ukrainian farmer watches as patches of his wheat fields burn (AP file photo)

Research underway in Ukraine

Early findings are encouraging

More than four years of war have left lasting damage across parts of Ukraine. It has not only affected buildings and infrastructure, but also the natural environment. Areas that once supported forests, wildlife and agriculture have been reduced to barren lands which could take years to recover.Ukraine's rich black soil has long been one of the country's biggest strengths. This natural asset helped the European nation become one of the world's leading producers and exporters of grain. Years of war have left it damaged and polluted, making farming difficult in some places.Researchers at the Jan Evangelista Purkyne University (UJEP) in the Czech Republic are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing grass, to see if it can gradually remove harmful pollutants from contaminated soil while also producing biomass that can be used for energy.The research is part of a NATO-backed project that aims to reduce the environmental damage caused by military conflict. Scientists say the process is slow and could take years, but early findings suggest the grass may improve soil health and prepare damaged land for future farming.Ukraine is often called the 'breadbasket of Europe' because of its vast areas of chernozem or black soil. The soil is rich in nutrients and organic matter, making it one of the most fertile soils in the world.It has helped Ukraine become a major producer of wheat, maize and other crops.However, after nearly four-and-a-half years of war, large areas of farmland have been affected by military activity. Soil in some regions has been polluted by oil products, explosives and other contaminants.Heavy vehicles, shelling and fighting have also damaged the land by compacting the soil and destroying vegetation. Restoring this land will be essential if it is to be used for agriculture again.At an experimental site on a former brown coal mine near Most in northern Czech Republic, researchers are growing giant Miscanthus to understand how it behaves in damaged soil."The goal is to revitalise contaminated areas while producing biomass," UJEP environmental scientist Josef Trogl says, as quoted by news agency AFP.Giant Miscanthus is originally from East Asia but is now grown across Europe. It is mainly used as a biomass crop because its dried stems can be burned to produce heat and energy.Researchers believe the plant may also help clean polluted land through a natural process called phytoremediation.Scientists say the plant develops a large and deep root system. These roots can trap some harmful substances, including certain metals and other pollutants, while improving the condition of the soil.Ember Morrissey, a biologist at West Virginia University and co-author of a recent study on giant Miscanthus, says the grass is "capable of growing on degraded and contaminated soils and produces extensive root systems that can accumulate metals while simultaneously restoring soil organic matter."According to the researchers, most of the pollutants remain in the roots underground. The stems and leaves that grow above the ground stay largely clean and can still be harvested as biomass.The plant also improves soil quality in another important way. "The plant also sends up to 40% of organic material it produces through photosynthesis to the soil via its roots, which is way more than other farm plants," Trogl said.Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into food, releasing oxygen as a by-product. As giant Miscanthus grows, its deep roots store large amounts of carbon in the soil. Scientists say this helps restore soil organic matter and gradually improves soil health over time.Healthy soil contains organic matter called humus, which helps retain water and nutrients needed for plant growth. Trogl says giant Miscanthus encourages the formation of humus more effectively than many other crops."The development of humus and soil fertility is better here than under other plants," he said, adding that the grass also supports soil microorganisms to faster degrade organic pollutants such as petroleum.Soil microorganisms are tiny living organisms, including bacteria and fungi, that naturally break down harmful substances. By creating better conditions for these organisms, the plant may help speed up the recovery of contaminated land.The Czech research is not limited to laboratory testing. Since 2023, scientists have also been growing giant Miscanthus in Vorzel, near Bucha, a suburb of Kyiv.The area was occupied by Russian forces between February and March 2022 before being liberated the following month. It was later cleared of mines during autumn 2022.According to Valentina Pidlisnyuk, a Ukraine-born professor at UJEP who leads the research team, the land suffered extensive environmental damage."The area was occupied by Russian troops between February and March 2022, liberated in April 2022, and subsequently demined in autumn 2022," she said.Although the grass takes several years to show its full impact, scientists say the first results are positive. Pidlisnyuk said analyses carried out so far have shown positive effects on soil biological parameters and carbon sequestration.Carbon sequestration means capturing and storing carbon in the soil instead of releasing it into the atmosphere. This not only improves soil quality but can also help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide contributing to climate change.Researchers say the project is giving them valuable information about how damaged land can be restored using natural methods instead of relying only on expensive engineering solutions.Worth €346,000 (around $395,000), the project involves researchers from the Czech Republic, Ukraine, Canada, Croatia, Kazakhstan and the United States. It is currently scheduled to continue until next year.
Article Summary: Ukraine's rich black soil has long been one of the country's biggest strengths. Years of war have left it damaged and polluted, making farming difficult in some places. Scientists are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing grass, to see if it can remove harmful pollutants from contaminated soil.

Article Title: CJP protest in Mumbai: Cop ‘inappropriately touches’ woman in video, stirs row
Article Text:
The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.





MUMBAI: A viral video from the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Thursday, showing a policeman allegedly inappropriately touching a woman protester, stirred up a fresh controversy on Friday, with the opposition demanding his dismissal.The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.DCP (operations) Akbar Pathan said, “The official was trying to hold on to a male protester and a lady stepped in while he was looking away. Senior officers have verified all the facts and minutely assessed the video to ascertain the facts,” he said.Another police official said, “Since the video went viral late Thursday night, our senior cyber crime experts carefully zoomed in on the footage, verified it, and found that there was no misconduct.”The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters that drugs would be planted on them and their career would be ruined if they continued participating in protests.The latest video quickly went viral on social media, with several opposition politicians demanding action against the policeman. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an apology from CM Devendra Fadnavis and dismissal of the policeman.In a post on X, Sapkal said, “The one who calls himself Devabhaau has turned out to be Duryodhan! Devabhaau’s police have become so rogue that they are violating the modesty of female students the age of their own daughters.”Mumbai Congress president and MP Varsha Gaikwad said, “What happened to a girl during the protest in Mumbai is deeply painful and disturbing. Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: 'Intense, highly unpredictable': Over 200,000 evacuated as massive wildfires engulf Spain, France
Article Text:
Spain, France battle devastating wildfires

More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors as massive wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.The fires prompted Spain to declare a national emergency, while French authorities ordered the complete evacuation, by land and sea, of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.Authorities in south-west France ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast "village by village" as an "intense, highly unpredictable" wildfire scorched more than 19,000 hectares (47,000 acres) of forest.In Spain, the government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two major blazes merged outside Madrid, while a third fire was close to joining them amid extreme heat and tinder-dry conditions across much of southern Europe.Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the blaze as the "worst fire in the history of the region", saying the area was facing a "perfect storm" of high temperatures, relentless winds and converging fire fronts.Local emergency services said the wildfires were advancing towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Oliva, about 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the Spanish capital."The wildfire is at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain," Carlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, said, as cited by the BBC."It's not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken," he added.A national emergency, which allows Spain's central government to assume powers and responsibilities normally held by the country's autonomous regions, has been declared only once before — during the nationwide blackout in April 2025.In south-west France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires tore through the Gironde and Landes regions.In the early hours of Saturday, authorities ordered the precautionary evacuation of four towns near Bordeaux: Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, Saint-Jean-d'Illac, Martignas-sur-Jalles and Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc. According to Le Monde, the four municipalities have a combined population of about 58,400.In 2022, a wildfire in south-west France scorched more than 30,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of 50,000 people. Fueled by dry conditions and strong winds, the latest blazes have swept through coastal pine forests, with flames reaching up to 10 metres (30 feet) high.French president Emmanuel Macron said he had activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism as the country battled multiple wildfires after enduring three successive heatwaves since May.Scientists say climate change is making extreme weather events more frequent and more intense by drying out soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and contributing to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is warming at nearly twice the global average rate.
Article Summary: Spanish government declares first-ever national emergency over wildfire. French authorities order complete evacuation of one of country's most popular holiday destinations. More than 200,000 people either fled or were ordered to remain indoors as wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.
